lessons.title: Take Objects Away
lessons.concept: Removing a Part from a Whole

play.shortDesc: Touch the named part to take it away, then count what is left
play.targetObjective: Take away a part and find what remains.
stepByStep: Look at the whole group.
Touch exactly the number being taken away.
Count the objects that remain.
play.kidTip: Take away only the amount named in the question.
play.audioPrompt: Take objects away. Touch the part that leaves, then find how many remain.

prompts.default: Take away {b}. How many {item} are left?

lessons.pedagogyTip: The crossed-out objects remain visible so subtraction means a change to one whole, not a second unrelated count.

lessons.title: Count What Remains
lessons.concept: Counting Only the Remaining Part

play.shortDesc: Skip the crossed-out objects and count only what remains
play.targetObjective: Count the remaining objects once each.
stepByStep: Notice which objects are already crossed out.
Touch only the objects that remain.
The last number you say is the difference.
play.kidTip: The crossed-out objects are gone. Count only what is still here.
play.audioPrompt: Count what remains. Skip every crossed-out object.

prompts.default: Count only the {item} that remain.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Separating the removal action from the final count helps children understand that the answer names the remaining set.

lessons.title: Separate a Part
lessons.concept: A Whole Made of Two Parts

play.shortDesc: Move one named part away and see the two parts of the whole
play.targetObjective: Separate the whole into a removed part and a remaining part.
stepByStep: Start with the whole group.
Move the named part into the separated area.
The objects still in the whole area are the other part.
play.kidTip: Move the named part away from the whole.
play.audioPrompt: Separate a part. Move the named part away and look at the part that remains.

prompts.default: Move {b} {item} into the separated part.

lessons.pedagogyTip: This keeps subtraction connected to part–whole composition: neither part disappears from the relationship when one moves away.

lessons.title: Match Groups to Compare
lessons.concept: Finding the Extra Objects by One-to-One Matching

play.shortDesc: Pair one object from each group and count what has no partner
play.targetObjective: Match the groups to reveal their difference.
stepByStep: Choose one object in the larger group.
Match it with one object in the smaller group.
When the smaller group is used, count what is unmatched.
play.kidTip: A matched pair uses one object from each group.
play.audioPrompt: Match the groups. Make pairs, then count the objects with no partner.

prompts.default: Match the groups. How many are unmatched?

lessons.pedagogyTip: One-to-one matching makes comparison subtraction a measured gap, not an instruction to remove from the larger set.

lessons.title: Read a Subtraction Equation
lessons.concept: Connecting a Removal Model to Symbols

play.shortDesc: Choose the equation whose whole, removed part, and remainder match the model
play.targetObjective: Read a removal action as a subtraction equation.
stepByStep: Read how many the model started with.
Read how many were removed.
Choose the equation with that start, change, and remainder.
play.kidTip: The first number is the whole; the second is what left.
play.audioPrompt: Read the subtraction equation. Match the start, the part removed, and what remains.

prompts.default: Choose the equation that matches the picture.

lessons.pedagogyTip: The minus sign gains meaning only after its three quantities are grounded in an action the child can already explain.

lessons.title: Count Back
lessons.concept: Moving Back for a Small Subtrahend

play.shortDesc: Start at the whole and say one earlier number for each part taken away
play.targetObjective: Count backward once for each object removed.
stepByStep: Say the starting number without recounting it.
Move back one number for each step.
Stop after the named number of backward steps.
play.kidTip: Each tap is one step backward, never forward.
play.audioPrompt: Count back. Start at the whole and move backward one step at a time.

prompts.default: Start at {a} and count back {b}.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Counting back is deliberately limited to one, two, or three steps; larger subtrahends need more efficient strategies rather than longer counting chains.

lessons.title: Subtract Zero
lessons.concept: Taking Away Nothing Changes Nothing

play.shortDesc: See that taking away none leaves the starting amount unchanged
play.targetObjective: Subtracting zero leaves a number unchanged.
stepByStep: Begin with the starting number.
Zero means no objects leave.
Choose the same number you started with.
play.kidTip: Taking away zero changes nothing.
play.audioPrompt: Subtract zero. Nothing leaves, so the starting number stays the same.

prompts.default: What is {a} minus zero?

lessons.pedagogyTip: Showing the unchanged quantity prevents the brittle shortcut that zero itself must always be the answer.

lessons.title: Subtract All
lessons.concept: Taking Away the Whole Leaves Zero

play.shortDesc: Take away an amount equal to the whole and see that none remain
play.targetObjective: A number minus itself is zero.
stepByStep: Compare the whole with the amount being removed.
Every object belongs to the removed part.
No object remains, so choose zero.
play.kidTip: Taking away all leaves none.
play.audioPrompt: Subtract all. When the whole group leaves, how many remain?

prompts.default: What is {a} minus {b}?

lessons.pedagogyTip: Subtracting all is the complementary zero rule: the equal operands matter, not merely the appearance of a zero.

lessons.title: Subtract One
lessons.concept: One Less Is the Previous Number

play.shortDesc: Move to the previous counting number when one is taken away
play.targetObjective: One less is the number immediately before.
stepByStep: Say the starting number.
Take one backward step.
The number just before it is one less.
play.kidTip: One less is the previous number.
play.audioPrompt: Subtract one. Say the number immediately before the starting number.

prompts.default: What is one less than {a}?

lessons.pedagogyTip: Linking one less to the counting sequence turns a memorised fact into a reusable relationship.

lessons.title: Use Your Fingers
lessons.concept: Lowering Fingers to Model Taking Away

play.shortDesc: Raise the whole on your fingers, lower the removed part, and count what remains
play.targetObjective: Model subtraction with fingers you raise and lower.
stepByStep: Raise the starting number of fingers.
Lower the number being taken away.
Count the fingers that stay raised.
play.kidTip: Lower only the fingers being taken away.
play.audioPrompt: Use your fingers. Raise the whole, lower the part taken away, and count what stays up.

prompts.default: Show {a} fingers. Lower {b}. How many stay up?

lessons.pedagogyTip: Fingers make the whole, removed part, and remainder simultaneously visible; they are a legitimate model, not a habit to hide.

lessons.title: Subtract in a Five-Frame
lessons.concept: Seeing What Remains within Five

play.shortDesc: Remove counters while keeping the five-frame pattern visible
play.targetObjective: Take counters from a five-frame and read what remains.
stepByStep: See the starting number in the row of five.
Take out the named number of counters.
Read the pattern that remains without rearranging it.
play.kidTip: Keep the frame in its row. Take counters out without moving the others.
play.audioPrompt: Five-frame subtraction. Take counters out and read how many remain.

prompts.default: Take {b} counters out of the five-frame. How many remain?

lessons.pedagogyTip: The fixed row lets a child see a remainder as its distance from five, while the faint removed marks preserve the starting quantity.

lessons.title: Subtract in a Ten-Frame
lessons.concept: Seeing What Remains within Ten

play.shortDesc: Remove counters from two rows of five and read the remaining pattern
play.targetObjective: Use the five-and-five structure to subtract within ten.
stepByStep: Read the starting counters in rows of five.
Take out the named number without moving the others.
Use the full row and empty spaces to see the remainder.
play.kidTip: A full row is five. Keep that structure while counters leave.
play.audioPrompt: Ten-frame subtraction. Remove the named counters and read what is left.

prompts.default: Take {b} counters out of the ten-frame. How many remain?

lessons.pedagogyTip: A ten-frame turns subtraction facts into recognisable five-and-ten relationships instead of another count from one.

lessons.title: Find the Missing Part
lessons.concept: Whole and Parts in Subtraction

play.shortDesc: Use the whole and one known part to find the other part
play.targetObjective: Find the missing part that completes a whole.
stepByStep: Read the whole at the top of the bond.
Read the known removed part below it.
Choose the remaining part that makes both parts equal the whole.
play.kidTip: The two parts must make the whole.
play.audioPrompt: Complete the number bond. Use the whole and one part to find the missing part.

prompts.default: {a} is the whole. One part is {b}. What is the missing part?

lessons.pedagogyTip: The labels keep operand roles stable: the subtrahend is the removed part and the difference is the remaining part, even when a different box is unknown later.

lessons.title: Move Back on a Number Path
lessons.concept: Backward Unit Jumps from the Minuend

play.shortDesc: Start at the whole and keep every one-step backward jump visible
play.targetObjective: Move backward one number for each unit subtracted.
stepByStep: Find the minuend on the numbered path.
Make one backward jump for each unit being subtracted.
The number where you stop is the difference.
play.kidTip: Backward jumps make the number smaller.
play.audioPrompt: Move back on the number path. Start at the whole and jump left once for each unit taken away.

prompts.default: Start at {a} and move back {b}.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Numbered unit intervals connect object removal to movement while retaining every jump as visible mathematical working.

lessons.title: Subtract on an Open Number Line
lessons.concept: Backward Jumps without Printed Intermediate Numbers

play.shortDesc: Make a backward jump and calculate its unlabelled landing point
play.targetObjective: Track subtraction on an open number line.
stepByStep: Mark the minuend as the starting point.
Jump left by the subtrahend.
Work out the landing value because the open line does not print it.
play.kidTip: The line is open, so keep the landing number in your head.
play.audioPrompt: Use an open number line. Jump backward from the minuend and work out where you land.

prompts.default: Start at {a}. Jump back {b}. Where do you land?

lessons.pedagogyTip: Removing intermediate labels shifts the work from reading a scale to calculating and recording a purposeful jump.

lessons.title: Count Up to Find the Difference
lessons.concept: Measuring the Gap between Two Numbers

play.shortDesc: Start at the smaller number and count forward to measure a short gap
play.targetObjective: Count up when the difference is small.
stepByStep: Start at the subtrahend, the smaller endpoint.
Count forward until you reach the minuend.
Count the jumps—the distance—not the landing number.
play.kidTip: Count the distance, not the number you land on.
play.audioPrompt: Count up to find the difference. Start at the smaller number and measure the short gap.

prompts.default: Start at {b}. Count up to {a}. How big is the difference?

lessons.pedagogyTip: For 83 minus 79, four forward counts are more efficient and less error-prone than seventy-nine backward counts; the number shape should choose the strategy.

lessons.title: Use Fact Families
lessons.concept: Four Equations from One Part–Whole Relationship

play.shortDesc: Build two addition and two subtraction equations from the same whole and parts
play.targetObjective: Write all four facts in a part–whole family.
stepByStep: Identify the whole and its two parts.
Write both addition orders with the whole as their total.
Write both subtractions with the whole first, then check all four together.
play.kidTip: The same three numbers make two additions and two subtractions.
play.audioPrompt: Use a fact family. Build two additions and two subtractions from the same three numbers.

prompts.default: {b}, {difference}, and {a} make a fact family. Complete all four facts.

lessons.pedagogyTip: One Check keeps the four equations as one relationship; scoring each blank separately would turn a structural idea into four unrelated quiz items.

lessons.title: Think Addition
lessons.concept: Subtraction as a Missing-Addend Question

play.shortDesc: Turn whole minus part into a known part plus a missing part
play.targetObjective: Use addition to find an unknown subtraction difference.
stepByStep: Keep the subtrahend as the known part.
Choose the addition equation that reaches the minuend whole.
Find the missing addend; it is also the subtraction difference.
play.kidTip: Think: known part plus what makes the whole?
play.audioPrompt: Think addition. Turn the subtraction into a missing-addend equation, then find the missing part.

prompts.default: {a} minus {b}. Which addition equation finds the missing part?

lessons.pedagogyTip: The inverse relationship makes subtraction answerable from facts the child already knows and prepares unknown-position equations without keyword shortcuts.

lessons.title: Use Doubles to Subtract
lessons.concept: An Equal Part Removed from Its Double

play.shortDesc: Use a known double to see what remains when one equal part is removed
play.targetObjective: Undo a doubles fact with subtraction.
stepByStep: Read the known double as two equal parts.
Remove one of those equal parts from the whole.
The other equal part remains.
play.kidTip: A double has two equal parts.
play.audioPrompt: Use doubles to subtract. The whole has two equal parts, so remove one and read the other.

prompts.default: Use the double to solve {a} minus {b}.

lessons.pedagogyTip: The displayed addition fact is the reason, not decorative help: if n plus n makes two n, removing either n must leave the other.

lessons.title: Recall Facts from Five
lessons.concept: The Partners That Make Five

play.shortDesc: Say what is left from five, then let the frame confirm the partner
play.targetObjective: Recall the subtraction facts from five.
stepByStep: Hold the five-frame in your mind, full.
Say how many are left when the named part goes.
Watch the frame cross them out and check your answer.
play.kidTip: Remember the partners that make five.
play.audioPrompt: Recall facts from five. Say what is left, then check the frame.

prompts.default: Five take away {b}. How many are left?

lessons.pedagogyTip: The frame answers second on purpose: a child who can already see the counters is counting, not recalling, and level 11 has taught that counting already.

lessons.title: Recall Facts from Ten
lessons.concept: The Partners That Make Ten

play.shortDesc: Say the partner of ten from memory, then let the frame confirm it
play.targetObjective: Recall the subtraction facts from ten.
stepByStep: Picture the full ten-frame.
Say the partner that goes with the named part.
Let the frame cross them out and check your answer.
play.kidTip: The two partners of ten always make ten.
play.audioPrompt: Recall facts from ten. Say the partner, then check the frame.

prompts.default: Ten take away {b}. How many are left?

lessons.pedagogyTip: Complements of ten are the same relationship the child met making ten in addition, so this reuses that concept key rather than opening a second record for it.

lessons.title: Bridge Through Ten
lessons.concept: Landing on Ten Before Subtracting the Rest

play.shortDesc: Jump back to ten first, then subtract whatever is left of the part
play.targetObjective: Split a subtrahend so one jump lands on ten.
stepByStep: Work out how far the whole is above ten.
Jump back that far to land exactly on ten.
Subtract the rest of the part from ten.
play.kidTip: Land on ten first; the rest is easier from there.
play.audioPrompt: Bridge through ten. Jump back to ten, then subtract what is left of the part.

prompts.default: {a} minus {b}. Jump back through ten.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Ten is the landmark that makes the second jump a known fact, which is why the split is chosen by the numbers rather than always cutting the part in half.

lessons.title: Bridge Through One Hundred
lessons.concept: Landing on a Hundred Before Subtracting the Rest

play.shortDesc: Use one hundred as the landmark, then subtract the remaining part
play.targetObjective: Split a subtrahend so one jump lands on one hundred.
stepByStep: Find how far the whole is above one hundred.
Jump back that far to land exactly on one hundred.
Subtract the rest of the part from one hundred.
play.kidTip: One hundred is the landmark; land there first.
play.audioPrompt: Bridge through one hundred. Land on the hundred, then subtract the rest.

prompts.default: {a} minus {b}. Jump back through one hundred.

lessons.pedagogyTip: The same bridging move at a larger place value shows the strategy belongs to the structure of the number system, not to the numbers under twenty where it was learned.

lessons.title: Use a Known Fact
lessons.concept: Deriving a Fact from Its Neighbour

play.shortDesc: Pick a fact you already know that is one step away, then adjust once
play.targetObjective: Derive an unknown fact from a known neighbour.
stepByStep: Find the offered fact with the same whole, one step from this one.
Read the answer you already know.
Adjust it by one in the right direction.
play.kidTip: Use a nearby fact, then adjust by one.
play.audioPrompt: Use a known fact. Choose the fact one step away, then adjust your answer by one.

prompts.default: {a} minus {b}. Which nearby fact helps?

lessons.pedagogyTip: Taking one more away makes the answer one smaller, and one fewer makes it one larger; naming that direction is the whole lesson, so the offered facts never include the target itself.

lessons.title: Subtract a Friendly Number, Then Adjust
lessons.concept: Rounding the Part Up and Giving Back the Extra

play.shortDesc: Take away the next whole ten, then hand back the extra you took
play.targetObjective: Subtract a friendly number and compensate.
stepByStep: Round the part up to the next ten.
Jump back by that friendly number.
Jump forward by the extra you took away.
play.kidTip: You took too much, so give the extra back.
play.audioPrompt: Subtract a friendly number, then adjust. Take the whole ten, then give back the extra.

prompts.default: {a} minus {b}. Subtract a friendly ten, then adjust.

lessons.pedagogyTip: The forward jump is the lesson: taking away too much has to be undone in the opposite direction, which is what separates compensation from a guess.

lessons.title: Keep the Same Difference
lessons.concept: Shifting Both Numbers by the Same Amount

play.shortDesc: Slide both numbers up together until the part becomes a friendly ten
play.targetObjective: Keep a difference unchanged by shifting both operands.
stepByStep: Work out what the part needs to reach the next ten.
Add that same amount to both numbers.
Subtract the new friendly pair; the gap has not moved.
play.kidTip: Move both numbers the same, and the gap stays the same.
play.audioPrompt: Keep the same difference. Slide both numbers up by the same amount, then subtract.

prompts.default: {a} minus {b}. Shift both numbers to keep the same difference.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Changing only one operand changes the answer; the difference survives only because both endpoints move together, which the two arrows on the line are there to show.

lessons.title: Use Base-Ten Blocks
lessons.concept: Subtracting Whole Units of Each Place

play.shortDesc: Take whole rods and units off the desk, then read what is left
play.targetObjective: Subtract two-digit numbers with base-ten blocks.
stepByStep: Read how many rods and units the desk holds.
Take away the rods and units the question names.
Read the value of the blocks that remain.
play.kidTip: Rods come off with rods, units with units.
play.audioPrompt: Use base-ten blocks. Take away the rods and units, then read what remains.

prompts.default: {a} minus {b}. Take the blocks away.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Every column here already has enough to give, so the child meets the place-value structure before meeting the exchange that complicates it.

lessons.title: Use a Place-Value Chart
lessons.concept: Subtracting Column by Column

play.shortDesc: Line the digits up by place and subtract each column on its own
play.targetObjective: Record subtraction in a place-value chart.
stepByStep: Check that the digits line up under T and O.
Subtract the ones column.
Subtract the tens column, then read the answer row.
play.kidTip: Each column only uses its own two digits.
play.audioPrompt: Use a place-value chart. Subtract each column on its own.

prompts.default: {a} minus {b}. Fill the answer row of the chart.

lessons.pedagogyTip: The chart is the blocks with the pictures removed: the same columns, so a child who can move rods can see why the digits may not be mixed between them.

lessons.title: Subtract Multiples of Ten
lessons.concept: Whole Tens Taken from Whole Tens

play.shortDesc: Count in whole rods when nothing but tens is involved
play.targetObjective: Subtract multiples of ten within one hundred.
stepByStep: Notice the desk holds only ten-rods.
Take away the number of rods the question names.
Count the rods left in tens.
play.kidTip: Count the rods, then say them in tens.
play.audioPrompt: Subtract multiples of ten. Take whole rods away and count what is left in tens.

prompts.default: {a} minus {b}. Take away whole ten-rods.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Seven rods minus three rods is four rods, exactly as seven minus three is four; naming that likeness is what makes multiples of ten a known fact rather than a new one.

lessons.title: Subtract Multiples of One Hundred
lessons.concept: Whole Hundreds Taken from Whole Hundreds

play.shortDesc: Count in whole flats when nothing but hundreds is involved
play.targetObjective: Subtract multiples of one hundred within one thousand.
stepByStep: Notice the desk holds only hundred-flats.
Take away the number of flats the question names.
Count the flats left in hundreds.
play.kidTip: Count the flats, then say them in hundreds.
play.audioPrompt: Subtract multiples of one hundred. Take whole flats away and count what is left.

prompts.default: {a} minus {b}. Take away whole hundred-flats.

lessons.pedagogyTip: The same small fact reappears one place further left, which is the whole argument for place value and worth saying out loud rather than leaving to be noticed.

lessons.title: Subtract Tens, Then Ones
lessons.concept: Splitting a Subtrahend by Place on a Line

play.shortDesc: Jump back the tens and the ones as two separate moves
play.targetObjective: Subtract a two-digit number in two place-value jumps.
stepByStep: Split the part into its tens and its ones.
Jump back the tens.
Jump back the ones, in either order.
play.kidTip: Two jumps: the tens and the ones.
play.audioPrompt: Subtract tens, then ones. Split the part by place and make two jumps.

prompts.default: {a} minus {b}. Jump back the tens and the ones.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Either order lands on the same number, so this mode accepts both: insisting on tens first would teach a rule where the point is that place value makes the order free.

lessons.title: Subtract Hundreds, Tens, and Ones
lessons.concept: Three Columns, Each Subtracted Alone

play.shortDesc: Extend the chart to three columns without changing the method
play.targetObjective: Subtract three-digit numbers column by column.
stepByStep: Line the digits up under H, T and O.
Subtract the ones, then the tens, then the hundreds.
Read the whole answer row.
play.kidTip: A third column changes nothing about how each column works.
play.audioPrompt: Subtract hundreds, tens, and ones. Work each column on its own.

prompts.default: {a} minus {b}. Fill the answer row of the chart.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Adding a column is deliberately uneventful; a child who expects a new rule for hundreds has learned the chart as a procedure rather than as places.

lessons.title: Use Expanded Form
lessons.concept: Subtracting Each Place, Then Recombining

play.shortDesc: Break both numbers into parts, subtract each, then add the parts back
play.targetObjective: Subtract using expanded form.
stepByStep: Write each number as its tens and its ones.
Subtract the tens, then subtract the ones.
Add the two answers back together.
play.kidTip: Subtract the parts, then put them back together.
play.audioPrompt: Use expanded form. Subtract each part, then add the parts back together.

prompts.default: {a} minus {b}. Subtract each part, then put them back together.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Expanded form is the bridge to the vertical algorithm: it shows the same column work with the place values still written out, before they are compressed into single digits.

lessons.title: Check Subtraction with Addition
lessons.concept: Rebuilding the Whole to Test an Answer

play.shortDesc: Solve the subtraction, then add your answer back to test it
play.targetObjective: Check a difference by rebuilding the minuend.
stepByStep: Subtract to find the difference.
Add that difference to the part taken away.
If it rebuilds the whole, the answer is right.
play.kidTip: Adding your answer back should rebuild the whole.
play.audioPrompt: Check subtraction with addition. Solve it, then add your answer back to the part taken away.

prompts.default: {a} minus {b}. Solve it, then check it with addition.

lessons.pedagogyTip: A check a child can run alone is worth more than a correct answer they cannot test, and it reuses the inverse relationship rather than teaching a separate verification trick.

lessons.title: Subtract Left to Right
lessons.concept: Taking the Largest Place Away First

play.shortDesc: Work down from the biggest place, keeping a running total
play.targetObjective: Subtract left to right, one place at a time.
stepByStep: Take away the tens first.
Take that answer and subtract the ones.
The last total is the difference.
play.kidTip: Biggest place first, then work down.
play.audioPrompt: Subtract left to right. Take the biggest place away first, then work down.

prompts.default: {a} minus {b}. Subtract the biggest place first.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Mental arithmetic usually runs left to right while the written algorithm runs right to left; meeting both stops a child treating the written direction as the only lawful one.

lessons.title: Exchange One Ten for Ten Ones
lessons.concept: Opening a Rod When the Ones Run Out

play.shortDesc: Break one ten-rod into ten units when there are not enough ones
play.targetObjective: Exchange a ten for ten ones and keep the value.
stepByStep: Check whether the desk has enough units.
Break one ten-rod into ten units.
Now take away the units and the rods the question names.
play.kidTip: Ten units are worth exactly one rod.
play.audioPrompt: Exchange one ten for ten ones. Break a rod when there are not enough units.

prompts.default: {a} minus {b}. Break a ten before you take the units.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Composing a ten and decomposing one are different skills, so this earns its own concept key rather than reusing the one Addition's bundling wrote.

lessons.title: Exchange One Hundred for Ten Tens
lessons.concept: Opening a Flat When the Rods Run Out

play.shortDesc: Break one hundred-flat into ten rods when there are not enough tens
play.targetObjective: Exchange a hundred for ten tens and keep the value.
stepByStep: Check whether the desk has enough ten-rods.
Break one hundred-flat into ten rods.
Now take away the blocks the question names.
play.kidTip: Ten rods are worth exactly one flat.
play.audioPrompt: Exchange one hundred for ten tens. Break a flat when there are not enough rods.

prompts.default: {a} minus {b}. Break a hundred before you take the rods.

lessons.pedagogyTip: The same move one place further left, so a child can see that exchanging is a rule about the number system rather than a trick that only works with ones.

lessons.title: Use the Vertical Algorithm
lessons.concept: Recording an Exchange in Columns

play.shortDesc: Set the sum out in columns and write the exchange where it happened
play.targetObjective: Subtract in columns with one exchange.
stepByStep: Start at the ones column.
If the top digit is too small, exchange one from its left and write both changes.
Subtract each column and write the digit underneath.
play.kidTip: Start at the ones and work left.
play.audioPrompt: Use the vertical algorithm. Exchange where you need to, and write down what changed.

prompts.default: {a} minus {b}. Write it in columns and exchange once.

lessons.pedagogyTip: The crossed-out digit and its replacement are written in full because a small unexplained mark above a column is the point at which the algorithm stops meaning anything.

lessons.title: Use Cascading Regrouping
lessons.concept: Two Exchanges in One Subtraction

play.shortDesc: Exchange twice when both the ones and the tens run short
play.targetObjective: Subtract in columns with two exchanges.
stepByStep: Exchange into the ones and subtract them.
Now check the tens; they may be short too.
Exchange into the tens, then finish every column.
play.kidTip: One exchange can leave the next column short.
play.audioPrompt: Use cascading regrouping. Exchange into the ones, then check whether the tens need one too.

prompts.default: {a} minus {b}. This one needs two exchanges.

lessons.pedagogyTip: The second exchange is caused by the first, which is why the columns must be worked in order rather than scanned for trouble all at once.

lessons.title: Regroup Across a Zero
lessons.concept: Opening a Hundred to Reach the Ones

play.shortDesc: Open a hundred into tens first when the tens column is empty
play.targetObjective: Exchange through a zero column.
stepByStep: The ones are short, but the tens have nothing to give.
Open one hundred into ten tens first.
Now take one of those tens into the ones and subtract.
play.kidTip: An empty column has to be filled before it can give.
play.audioPrompt: Regroup across a zero. Open a hundred into ten tens first, then take one ten into the ones.

prompts.default: {a} minus {b}. Exchange through the zero.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Both exchanges are shown as separate written steps: compressing them into one move is exactly where children learn to produce the right digits without any idea what happened.

lessons.title: Estimate by Rounding
lessons.concept: An Answer That Is About Right

play.shortDesc: Round both numbers, then subtract the friendly pair
play.targetObjective: Estimate a difference by rounding.
stepByStep: Round each number to the nearest hundred.
Subtract the rounded numbers.
Say the answer as 'about', not as exact.
play.kidTip: An estimate is about, not exact.
play.audioPrompt: Estimate by rounding. Round both numbers, then subtract the friendly pair.

prompts.default: About how much is {a} minus {b}?

lessons.pedagogyTip: Neither number is already round, so rounding is real work rather than a step the question has done in advance.

lessons.title: Is the Answer Reasonable?
lessons.concept: Judging an Answer Against an Estimate

play.shortDesc: Estimate first, then decide whether a claimed answer can be right
play.targetObjective: Judge whether an answer is reasonable, and say why.
stepByStep: Round and estimate the answer for yourself.
Compare the claim with your estimate.
Choose the reason that explains the difference.
play.kidTip: Estimate first, then judge the claim.
play.audioPrompt: Is the answer reasonable? Estimate first, then decide whether the claim can be right.

prompts.default: Someone says {a} minus {b} is {claim}. Is that reasonable?

lessons.pedagogyTip: The wrong claims are the mistakes children actually make, so rejecting one takes a real estimate; an answer twenty times too big would be dismissed on sight without any estimating at all.

lessons.title: Find the Missing Part Taken Away
lessons.concept: The Unknown in the Middle of an Equation

play.shortDesc: Use the whole and what remains to find the part that left
play.targetObjective: Find a missing subtrahend.
stepByStep: Read the whole and the part that remains.
Find the gap between them.
That gap is the part that was taken away.
play.kidTip: Count up from what remains to the whole.
play.audioPrompt: Find the missing part taken away. Use the whole and what remains.

prompts.default: {a} is the whole and {difference} remains. What part was taken away?

lessons.pedagogyTip: Moving the unknown out of the answer position is what stops subtraction being read as an instruction to perform, and starts it being read as a relationship.

lessons.title: Find the Missing Whole
lessons.concept: Rebuilding a Whole from Both Parts

play.shortDesc: Put both parts back together to find where the subtraction started
play.targetObjective: Find a missing minuend.
stepByStep: Read the part taken away and the part that remains.
Join the two parts.
Their total is the whole you started with.
play.kidTip: Both parts together make the whole.
play.audioPrompt: Find the missing whole. Put the part taken away and the part left back together.

prompts.default: One part is {b} and the other is {difference}. What is the whole?

lessons.pedagogyTip: An unknown start is solved by adding, which is the clearest case of why keyword reading fails: the word is still 'left', but the operation is not subtraction.

lessons.title: Take Away: How Many Are Left?
lessons.concept: A Removal Story with the Result Unknown

templates: {who} picked {v0} {item}. Then {v1} of them blew away.

play.shortDesc: Model a story where something is taken away and the end amount is unknown
play.targetObjective: Model a take-away story with the result unknown.
stepByStep: Find the amount at the start.
Find the amount that left.
The bar that is left is the answer.
play.kidTip: The start, the change, and what is left are three different numbers.
play.audioPrompt: Take away, result unknown. Find how many are left at the end.

prompts.default: {who} had {v0} {item}. {who} gave {v1} away. How many are left?

lessons.pedagogyTip: The bar model is drawn before the answer is chosen so the child commits to a structure rather than to a guess about which operation the words imply.

lessons.title: Take Away: How Many Left the Group?
lessons.concept: A Removal Story with the Change Unknown

templates: {who} started with {v0} {item} and has {v1} left after {place} closed.
There were {v0} {item} on the shelf. Only {v1} are still there.

play.shortDesc: Model a story where the amount that left is the unknown
play.targetObjective: Model a take-away story with the change unknown.
stepByStep: Find the amount at the start.
Find the amount at the end.
The gap between them is what left.
play.kidTip: The missing number is the part that went away.
play.audioPrompt: Take away, change unknown. Work out how many left the group.

prompts.default: {who} had {v0} {item}. Now {who} has {v1}. How many were given away?

lessons.pedagogyTip: Nothing in the sentence says 'take away', yet the model is still removal — which is why the unknown's position must drive the model rather than the wording.

lessons.title: Take Away: How Many Were There?
lessons.concept: A Removal Story with the Start Unknown

templates: {v0} {item} were sold at {place}, and {v1} are still there.

play.shortDesc: Model a story where the starting amount is the unknown
play.targetObjective: Model a take-away story with the start unknown.
stepByStep: Find what was taken away.
Find what is left.
Put both parts back together to rebuild the start.
play.kidTip: Both parts together make the amount you started with.
play.audioPrompt: Take away, start unknown. Put the parts back together to find the beginning.

prompts.default: {who} gave away {v0} {item} and has {v1} left. How many were there to start with?

lessons.pedagogyTip: This is the clearest case against keyword reading: the story says 'gave away' and 'lost', and the child has to add.

lessons.title: Compare: How Many More?
lessons.concept: A Comparison Story with the Gap Unknown

play.shortDesc: Line two groups up and measure the gap without taking anything away
play.targetObjective: Model a comparison story with the difference unknown.
stepByStep: Draw one bar for each group.
Line them up at the same left edge.
Measure the gap where one bar is longer.
play.kidTip: Nobody gives anything away when we compare.
play.audioPrompt: Compare, difference unknown. Line the two groups up and measure the gap.

prompts.default: {who} has {v0} {item}. {other} has {v1}. How many more does one have than the other?

lessons.pedagogyTip: Comparison is where 'subtraction means take away' finally breaks: both groups keep everything they have, and the answer is a measured distance.

lessons.title: Compare: How Many Does the Bigger Group Have?
lessons.concept: A Comparison Story with the Larger Amount Unknown

templates: At {place}, {who} found {v0} {item}, and {other} found {v1} more than that.

play.shortDesc: Use the smaller group and the gap to find the larger group
play.targetObjective: Model a comparison story with the bigger amount unknown.
stepByStep: Draw the group you know.
Add the gap on to the end of it.
The longer bar is the group you are asked about.
play.kidTip: More than means the other bar is longer by the gap.
play.audioPrompt: Compare, bigger unknown. Add the gap to the group you already know.

prompts.default: {who} has {v0} {item}. {other} has {v1} more. How many does {other} have?

lessons.pedagogyTip: 'More' appears in the sentence and the answer is found by adding, which is correct here and wrong in the next lesson — the model, not the word, decides.

lessons.title: Compare: How Many Does the Smaller Group Have?
lessons.concept: A Comparison Story with the Smaller Amount Unknown

play.shortDesc: Use the larger group and the gap to find the smaller group
play.targetObjective: Model a comparison story with the smaller amount unknown.
stepByStep: Draw the group you know.
Mark the gap back from its end.
The shorter bar is the group you are asked about.
play.kidTip: Fewer than means the other bar is shorter by the gap.
play.audioPrompt: Compare, smaller unknown. Take the gap back from the group you know.

prompts.default: {who} has {v0} {item}. {other} has {v1} fewer. How many does {other} have?

lessons.pedagogyTip: Paired with level 49 on purpose: same shape, opposite operation, so the child has to read the relationship rather than hunt for a keyword.

lessons.title: Solve Two-Step Problems
lessons.concept: Two Changes, One After the Other

templates: {who} had {v0} {item}, then found {v1} more, then gave {v2} away.
At {place}, {who} started with {v0} {item}, was given {v1} more, and used {v2}.

play.shortDesc: Work through two changes in the order the story tells them
play.targetObjective: Solve a problem with two changes.
stepByStep: Work out the amount after the first change.
Apply the second change to that amount.
Only the final amount answers the question.
play.kidTip: Answer the first change before you touch the second.
play.audioPrompt: Solve a two-step problem. Take the changes one at a time, in order.

prompts.default: {who} had {v0} {item}, then found {v1} more, then gave {v2} away. How many are left?

lessons.pedagogyTip: The middle amount is asked for first and refused if wrong, because a child who jumps to the end has usually combined the two changes into one number that means nothing.

lessons.title: Explain and Compare Strategies
lessons.concept: Choosing the Method the Numbers Reward

play.shortDesc: Pick a method that suits these numbers, then compare it with another that works
play.targetObjective: Choose and justify a subtraction strategy.
stepByStep: Look at the two numbers before choosing anything.
Pick a method their shape rewards.
Compare it with another correct method and count the steps.
play.kidTip: Look at the numbers before you choose a method.
play.audioPrompt: Explain and compare strategies. Choose the way these numbers reward, then compare it with another that also works.

prompts.default: {a} minus {b}. Which way would you do it?

lessons.pedagogyTip: Every strategy that genuinely fits is accepted, and the comparison is between two correct paths: choosing between one right and one broken method is not strategy work, it is spotting an error.

lessons.title: Practice: Take Away and Compare
lessons.concept: Practice Without Help

play.shortDesc: Every way of taking objects away, mixed and unaided
play.targetObjective: Retrieve every object-level subtraction without help.
play.kidTip: No hints here — try what you remember.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Retrieval without scaffolding is a different act from being walked through a method, and it is the one that makes a technique stick.

lessons.title: Practice: Five and Ten Frames
lessons.concept: Practice Without Help

play.shortDesc: Build and recall inside both frames, mixed and unaided
play.targetObjective: Retrieve frame subtraction and the partners of five and ten.
play.kidTip: Some of these you build; some you just remember.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Mixing the building modes with the recall modes is the point: a child who can only answer when the counters are tappable has not learned the facts.

lessons.title: Practice: Number Bonds
lessons.concept: Practice Without Help

play.shortDesc: All three unknown positions in a part-whole bond, mixed
play.targetObjective: Solve a bond wherever the unknown sits.
play.kidTip: Check which box is empty before you start.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Cycling the unknown position stops a child answering by habit: the same three numbers ask a different question depending on which box is blank.

lessons.title: Practice: Related Facts
lessons.concept: Practice Without Help

play.shortDesc: Families, think-addition, doubles and derived facts, mixed
play.targetObjective: Retrieve and derive subtraction facts without help.
play.kidTip: Use whatever fact you already know.

lessons.pedagogyTip: The four modes are four routes to the same recall, so mixing them asks the child to choose a route rather than follow the one the lesson just taught.

lessons.title: Practice: Number Lines
lessons.concept: Practice Without Help

play.shortDesc: Every jump strategy on the line, mixed and unaided
play.targetObjective: Choose and carry out the right jumps without help.
play.kidTip: Look at the numbers before you jump.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Eight strategies in one round is where the child stops being told which one to use and starts reading the numbers for themselves.

lessons.title: Practice: Base-Ten Blocks
lessons.concept: Practice Without Help

play.shortDesc: Clean columns, whole units and exchanges, mixed
play.targetObjective: Subtract with blocks, exchanging only when the desk needs it.
play.kidTip: Check whether the desk can pay before you take.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Half these questions need an exchange and half do not, so the child has to check rather than reach for the trade every time.

lessons.title: Practice: Place Value Charts
lessons.concept: Practice Without Help

play.shortDesc: Charts, expanded form, checking and left-to-right, mixed
play.targetObjective: Record subtraction by place in every written form taught.
play.kidTip: Each column keeps its own two digits.

lessons.pedagogyTip: The same arithmetic in four notations, so place value is the thing being practised rather than one layout.

lessons.title: Practice: Column Subtraction
lessons.concept: Practice Without Help

play.shortDesc: One exchange, two exchanges, and exchanging across a zero
play.targetObjective: Run the written algorithm on every exchange shape.
play.kidTip: Start at the ones and write every exchange down.

lessons.pedagogyTip: The three shapes are indistinguishable until the ones column is reached, so mixing them forces the child to work rather than to recognise the lesson.

lessons.title: Practice: Estimation
lessons.concept: Practice Without Help

play.shortDesc: Estimate a difference, then judge someone else's answer
play.targetObjective: Estimate and judge without help.
play.kidTip: About, not exact.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Producing an estimate and judging one are different skills; alternating them stops the second becoming a guess about which button is nicer.

lessons.title: Practice: Story Problems
lessons.concept: Practice Without Help

play.shortDesc: All seven story shapes, mixed, with no keyword to lean on
play.targetObjective: Model any subtraction story without help.
play.kidTip: Find the unknown before you choose what to do.

lessons.pedagogyTip: Mixed unknown positions are the only honest test of story work: with one shape per round a child can answer every question by copying the last one.

lessons.title: Practice: Choosing a Strategy
lessons.concept: Practice Without Help

play.shortDesc: Read the numbers and choose a method that suits them
play.targetObjective: Choose a fitting strategy unaided.
play.kidTip: The numbers decide, not habit.

lessons.pedagogyTip: One mode, but every question is different numbers: the practice is the reading, not the method.
